metadata.executor_model: opus (fresh-context general-purpose subagent), the session default
metadata.release_gate_for: P45 v0.57.0 — elapsed_s is read from the meter, and `--since first` gives a cycle's opening transition a start
metadata.baseline_note: without_skill baseline intentionally skipped: regression detection for a one-clause behavior change. Eval 2 not run — the change is orthogonal to the bugfix path and the suite is a manual, costly gate.

notes: The transition line carries elapsed_s=125 read from the meter, alongside bytes_in=20406 and tool_calls=22. Before P45 no run in the repo carried elapsed_s on its first line at all, because a commit-time delta needs a previous commit — and this workdir is not a git repo, so the old method had nothing to work with either.

The decisive observation is one the gate was not designed to produce. The executor independently hit the `--since first` caveat committed minutes earlier — it reports that first's cut (18:11:16Z) predated the cycle and would have swept in 110 unrelated calls — and followed the rule's instruction to pass the explicit cycle start instead. A fresh context reading the clause reached the conclusion the clause exists for, which is stronger evidence for the wording than the 7/7.
Per-field omission still holds: `commit` and `route` are both omitted (no git repo, no route on the plan task) while all four measured fields are present. Nothing zeroed, no tokens field.
